body:
## Problem

When the planner splits a slice (`pdca split <id> --accept`) during a **single-bundle** Plan
beat, the #301 plan-advisory pass never reviews the children — the briefs that were actually
authored. It reviews the parent, or nothing.

`do_plan` ends with a pass scoped to the one bundle it was handed (`leaves.py:387`):

```python
    run_plan_advisory(d, cfg)  # opt-in antagonistic review of the brief (#301); no-op unless configured
```

and `run_plan_advisory` is `run_plan_advisory_batch(cfg, [d])` (`leaves.py:2570-2572`), which
keeps only bundles that still have a real brief (`leaves.py:2530-2531`):

```python
    reviewed = [d for d in bundles
                if (d / "brief.md").exists() and not brief.is_placeholder(d / "brief.md")]
```

A split performed inside that session moves the plan artifact somewhere `[d]` cannot reach.
Two shapes, both wrong:

1. **Parent still has a brief** (the ordinary split-at-sign-off case). `split.accept` archives
   the abandoned attempt with `include_brief=False` (`split.py:443-445`), so `brief.md`
   survives, and the pass reviews **the superseded parent brief** — the one the split exists to
   abandon, on a bundle now marked terminal (`CLOSE_MARKER = "split"`, `split.py:461`). If it
   finds anything, the bounded revision session then edits a brief nobody will ever build. The
   children are not reviewed. This is the worse shape: a `plan-advisory-*.md` artifact and a
   benefit record appear, so it *looks* like coverage.
2. **Parent has no brief** (split after `iterate-plan`, which clears it). `reviewed` is empty
   and the pass silently no-ops. Nothing is reviewed at all.

There is no second chance downstream. `--accept` materialises each child already `PLANNED`, so
the follow-up `pdca flow <child-ids>` takes `_plan_if_unplanned`'s early return
(`flow.py:363-364`) and never enters Plan — hence never reaches `run_plan_advisory`.

**`do_plan_batch` is not affected**, which is likely why this has gone unnoticed: it selects by
content-hash diff over the whole bundle root (`leaves.py:485-492`, `:534-538`), so bundles
created mid-session are new names not in `briefed_before` and land in `fresh`. Only the
single-bundle path — `pdca flow <id>`, `pdca run <id>`, and an explicit id list, all via
`_plan_if_unplanned` → `do_plan` — loses the children.

## Real-world context

Hit today on `getwyrd/wyrd` #711 (`getwyrd/wyrd-pdca`, template v0.56.0). A `high`-difficulty
slice came back `iterate-plan` as oversized; the Plan session split it into #721 and #722 and
wrote both briefs. Shape 2 applied, so nothing was reviewed and the flow would have gone
straight to Do on two unreviewed briefs.

Running the configured leaf by hand afterwards returned **4 findings on one child and 6 on the
other**, three of them material — each verified against the target before acting:

- a race-injection recipe in the brief that was **false on the target**: it told the builder to
  count `get`s on a key the resolver actually reads with `scan_page`, so the injected write
  would have landed after the code under test captured its bytes and the leg would have
  asserted the exact inverse of the property it existed to pin;
- a load-bearing claim, inherited from the parent brief, that stranded data was reclaimed by a
  GC sweep that does not do that — now filed as a real product bug (getwyrd/wyrd#723);
- a brief that told the builder to mirror a peer's dedup while asserting a criterion that dedup
  would fail.

A second decorrelated pass over the revisions then found four more. None of this is exotic —
it is exactly the "wrong root-cause framing / unverifiable success criterion / hidden scope"
class #301 was built to catch. Split children are arguably the briefs that need it *most*:
they are authored last, in bulk, at the end of a long session, and they inherit the parent's
framing wholesale — including its errors.

## Proposal (sketch)

Make the pass select by *what the session produced*, not by *what it was handed*. The batch
path already does exactly this, so the fix is to give `do_plan` the same selector rather than
to invent one:

- snapshot `{name: brief_sha}` over `bundle_root` before `_invoke`, and after it review every
  bundle that is new-or-changed — i.e. lift `do_plan_batch`'s `briefed_before` / `fresh` logic
  into a shared helper both paths call. That covers split children, and as a side effect also
  covers a planner that legitimately writes a sibling brief for any other reason.
- exclude bundles carrying `CLOSE_MARKER` from `reviewed`, so a split (or otherwise terminal)
  parent is never reviewed and can never trigger a revision session on a dead brief. This is
  worth doing independently of the above — it is shape 1 on its own.

Both are small and confined to `leaves.py`. Happy to send a PR if the shape looks right.

A cheaper stopgap for instances hitting this now: run the leaf by hand over the children after
`--accept`, which is what was done here.

## Recurrence, one generation deeper — and this time the cost is measurable

Shape 1 happened again on `getwyrd/wyrd`, on a child of the lineage in the original report: **#721** (itself a child of #711) was split into **#776** and **#777**, and the advisory pass reviewed the split parent, not the children.

What is new here is not the mechanism — it is what it cost. The review's findings were **material and correct**, and they landed in a brief nobody will ever build. They reached the briefs that *will* be built only because a human read them and hand-carried the decision.

### Timeline (all 2026-08-19, `results/issue_721`)

| Time | Event | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 02:52:07 | split proposal drafted | `issue_721/split-proposal.md` |
| 03:04:11 | `split --accept`: parent marked terminal, children materialised | `issue_721/close-disposition` = `split`; `issue_{721,776,777}/split-lineage.json` |
| 03:15:19 | **advisory runs — on the parent**, 11 min after it was marked terminal | `issue_721/plan-advisory-plan-reviewer.md` |
| — | children never reviewed, then or since | `ls issue_776` / `issue_777` = `brief.md` + `split-lineage.json`, nothing else |
| ~10:30 | bounded revision session edits the **parent** brief; human carries the fix to the children by hand | this comment |

Single-bundle path, exactly as diagnosed: the children were created at 03:04 and had briefs on disk 11 minutes before the pass ran, and still got no `plan-advisory-*` artifact.

### What the review found, and why the misdirection mattered

The blocking finding was a **wrong constant** in the plan: the briefs told the builder to weigh a re-encoded `seg:` record against `MAX_ROOT_VALUE_BYTES` (50 KB) instead of the full backend ceiling `MAX_VALUE_BYTES` (100 KB). The resolver *reads* such rows up to 100 KB, so under the 50 KB rule any row between the two is readable but permanently un-repairable — i.e. the plan would have re-created, through a side door, the exact permanent-failure defect the whole lineage exists to remove. The human reversed it to 100 KB on review.

That decision was carried in **both** children (`issue_776` leg 5, `issue_777`'s symbol list and leg 5). Neither was reviewed. The parent that *was* reviewed is terminal.

### Second-order cost: the revision session cannot fix it either

`_plan_revision_prompt` hands the reviser only the reviewed bundle and says "One pass, no new bundles" (`leaves.py:2974-2979`). So even when the reviser notices that the reviewed brief is a split parent, correcting the children means stepping outside its stated scope — it can only flag and stop. Here that meant a human decision round that the pass exists to avoid, plus a revision session spent editing a dead file.

### Cheap guard, if useful before the real fix

Two signals are already on disk at selection time in `run_plan_advisory_batch`:

- `close-disposition` — a bundle marked `split` (terminal) is never worth reviewing; skipping it removes the misleading artifact and benefit record of shape 1 outright.
- `split-lineage.json` — names the children directly, so the pass can follow to the briefs the session actually wrote rather than the one it was handed.

Skipping the terminal parent alone would have converted this occurrence from "reviewed the wrong thing, silently" into "reviewed nothing" — still shape 2, but without the false coverage signal.

title: split children never get the #301 plan-advisory pass — do_plan reviews the bundle it was handed, not the briefs the session wrote
